facts.statement: Teviornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Teviornis is an extinct genus of presbyornithid which lived during the Maastrichtian stage, around 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The time range for Teviornis is estimated between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Teviornis is considered the oldest known neognath bird, alongside Vegavis.
facts.quote: It is the oldest known neognath along with Vegavis

facts.statement: Fossils of Teviornis have been collected from the Nemegt Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: its fossils are collected from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia

facts.statement: The fossils were found at the Guriliin Tsav locality in the northwest corner of Umnogobi Aimak, Mongolia.
facts.quote: The fossils were collected at the Guriliin Tsav locality, northwest corner of Umnogobi Aimak, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a crushed partial right forelimb.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a crushed partial right forelimb.

facts.statement: The catalog number for the holotype fossils is PIN 4499–1.
facts.quote: The catalog number of these fossils are given multiple times as PIN 4499–1

facts.statement: The genus name Teviornis combines the Greek word for bird with the name of Victor Tereschenko, the paleontologist who discovered the specimen.
facts.quote: The genus name Teviornis is the Greek masculine word for bird combined with the name of Victor Tereschenko, the Paleontologist at the PIN who discovered the specimen.

facts.statement: The species name T. gobiensis refers to the Gobi Desert where the fossil was discovered.
facts.quote: The species name T. gobiensis refers to the harsh Gobi Desert in which the fossil was found.

facts.statement: The fossils are housed in the collection of the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow.
facts.quote: The fossils are in the collection of the Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow.

facts.statement: Teviornis was originally described in 2002 by Kurochkin, Dyke, and Karhu as a member of the family Presbyornithidae.
facts.quote: In 2002, Teviornis was described by Kurochkin, Dyke & Karhu as a member of the Presbyornithidae.

facts.statement: If Teviornis belongs to Presbyornithidae, it suggests that relatives of modern waterfowl were widespread and highly evolved by the end of the Mesozoic.
facts.quote: If Teviornis does belong to the Presbyornithidae then, together with Vegavis from Antarctica, there is evidence that relatives of today's waterfowl already were widespread and highly apomorphic by the end of the Mesozoic.

facts.statement: Clarke and Norell (2004) argued that characters originally used to assign Teviornis to Anseriformes, like an unbowed metacarpal III, are primitive traits retained in other bird groups.
facts.quote: Clarke and Norell reviewed the specimen in 2004. They concluded that some of the characters used by Kurochkin et al. to assign T. gobiensis to the Anseriformes, such as an unbowed metacarpal III, are plesiomorphies which are primitive for Avialae and also retained in some members of Ornithurae.

facts.statement: A 2016 study by De Pietri and colleagues confirmed Teviornis as a presbyornithid based on features like the trochlea carpalis extension.
facts.quote: In 2016, De Pietri and colleagues reassessed the type specimen of Teviornis and confirmed the taxon's identity as a presbyornithid on the basis of the trochlea carpalis extension

facts.statement: A 2019 study supports the classification of presbyornithids as stem anseriforms.
facts.quote: A 2019 study also supports the placement of presbyornithids as stem anseriforms.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses have produced conflicting results, with a 2023 study placing Teviornis as a presbyornithid and a 2025 study placing it as a basal ornithurine.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis showed different results: the 2023 study placed Teviornis as a presbyornithid, while the 2025 study placed Teviornis as a basal ornithurine.

facts.statement: The fossil site where Teviornis was found also yielded remains of Tarbosaurus, Gallimimus, Oksoko, Saurolophus, Prenocephale, and Gurilynia.
facts.quote: Other dinosaurs recovered from Gurillin Tsav include the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus, the ornithomimid Gallimimus, the oviraptorid Oksoko, the hadrosaurid Saurolophus, the pachycephalosaurid Prenocephale and the enantiornithine Gurilynia.

facts.statement: The same locality also contained fossils of the turtle Mongolochelys, an azhdarchid pterosaur, and a metatherian mammal.
facts.quote: Other animals from the same locality include the sichuanchelyid turtle Mongolochelys, the azhdarchid pterosaur and the metatherian mammal (Gurlin Tsav skull).

rejected.statement: Clarke and Norell concluded that Teviornis cannot be confidently assigned to Presbyornithidae because no unique shared traits were found in the specimen.
rejected.quote: Moreover, Clarke and Norell found no synapomorphies of Aves (sensu Gauthier), Neognathae, or Galloanseres, preserved in PIN 4499–1, so they concluded that Teviornis cannot be confidently assigned to the Presbyornithidae.
